finding.claim: Ruby exceptions raised inside SQLite callbacks (collation comparator, authorizer, busy handler, trace, aggregator finalize) are not caught by rb_protect, so they longjmp through sqlite3_step's C frames with no cleanup. A comparator that raises on attacker-written row text leaves the connection and VDBE state inconsistent.
finding.source: Attacker-written row text passed as a_str/b_str to the collation comparator (database.c:827-829)
finding.sink: rb_funcall(comparator, "compare") at database.c:839, unprotected, inside sqlite3_step

trace.note: rb_comparator_func invoked by SQLite for COLLATE comparisons
rb_funcall to application comparator, no rb_protect
NUM2INT on comparator return value, can also raise
errinfo re-raise path is never reached because the longjmp bypasses it

finding.guards_checked: rb_protect used only at ext/sqlite3/aggregator.c:47 and ext/sqlite3/database.c:581 (rb_sqlite3_func). No protection on collation, authorizer (database.c:738), busy handler (database.c:365), trace (database.c:328), or aggregator finalize set_sqlite3_func_result (aggregator.c:164). rb_str_export_to_enc (database.c:835-836) does not raise. Exploit requires an application comparator that raises on the input; not executed.

finding.claim: statement_timeout= ignores the configured milliseconds. The progress callback never reads stmt_timeout, so any statement executing more than about 2000 VM steps is interrupted with SQLITE_INTERRUPT regardless of the configured value.
finding.source: Application-supplied ms value to statement_timeout= (database.c:437-442); not attacker-settable
finding.sink: Progress callback interrupt decision at database.c:422-423
finding.guards_checked: None relevant. Logic error in the timeout computation; the configured duration is never compared.

finding.claim: step() treats any non-nil rb_errinfo() as a callback exception. Ruby's $! is non-nil inside rescue/ensure, so a successful step called from a rescue block re-raises the rescued exception, discards the rows, and clears $!.
finding.source: Ruby $! (ec->errinfo) set by an exception the application is handling, e.g. an attacker-triggered validation error
finding.sink: rb_exc_raise of the stale exception at statement.c:147-149, plus rb_set_errinfo(Qnil) at statement.c:148

trace.note: rb_errinfo() != Qnil because caller is inside rescue

finding.guards_checked: No check distinguishes a callback exception from an unrelated $!. Relies on Ruby C-API semantics; not executed. Ruby-level execute wrappers are not in the tree.

finding.claim: execute_batch2 returns text truncated at the first embedded NUL (rb_str_new_cstr), while step() returns the full length-delimited value. Attacker-stored text such as 'admin\0x' reads back as 'admin' through exec_batch.
finding.source: Attacker-written text containing a NUL byte, stored in full by SQLite
finding.sink: Row values returned by exec_batch to the application (database.c:943-945, 962-964)

trace.note: exec_batch drives sqlite3_exec with these callbacks
contrast: step uses sqlite3_column_bytes, no truncation

finding.guards_checked: None in the binding. Impact depends on the application using execute_batch2 for lookups or authorization; not verified.
